terra.problem: It asserts what the writer wants readers to see, though the passage does not state his intent.
Papa Dorin comments on how he is presenting the passage: 'I'm pointing at it too.'
Pilate's role as governor is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The explanation repeats the same point in a flat, generic way without adding much after the second sentence.
'Wrong rank' uses 'wrong' about the baker's answer.
The passage calls the tomb cut out of rock; it does not describe it as a built space.
'The next stop' refers to the lesson's structure, which Papa Dorin does not discuss.
The claim that the stone cannot move without help adds a detail the passage does not give.
The joke assumes a log would be small, but a log can be large. The comparison does not reliably make sense.
'They won't forget that place' asserts what the women will remember, which the passage does not say.
'So they can finally go' adds a reason for the timing that the passage does not give.
Cinnamon is a food mentioned in a joke, not a food named in the passage.
'Nobody in the group has an answer yet' asserts more than the passage says. It records their question, not whether anyone had an answer.
'Soldiers aren't on their minds' asserts what the women are thinking without marking it as a guess.
It says all the women already know which tomb, but the cited verse identifies only Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joseph as seeing where the body was placed.
Their question was who would roll the stone away. The passage does not identify who did it.
The passage does not say the women expected nobody to be inside the tomb.
'Wrong guy' uses 'wrong' about the baker's answer.
'Same linen idea' suggests the young man's robe was linen, but the passage only says it was white.
'You only say that to people who are already alarmed' is an unsupported generalization.
'Delight hasn't hit yet' suggests the women later become delighted, which this passage does not say.
The young man tells them to see the place, but the passage does not say he points.
The young man's words do not state that nobody moved the body. They say Jesus has risen and is not there.
The description of Galilee as a northern region where Jesus did much teaching brings in facts from outside the passage without a reference.
'Wrong road' uses 'wrong' about the baker's answer.
The passage says the women said nothing to anyone in their fear; it does not place them on a road.
